The trip record also timestamps the deviation and rejoin, so the record establishes both the fact and the size of the deviation without any inference.

The driver's device trace measures only 12.318 km over 53 fixes, and the temptation is to say the route was short. POL-RD-22 forecloses that: the trace shows which route was taken and when, but is not used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The recorded 14.6 km and 12.7 km govern, and the 1.90 km deviation stands on those figures.

The LTA record for the recommended route itself — Ayer Rajah Expressway, towards City, from Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct, overlapping the trip window — is advisory type NONE, with speed bands 4 to 6 and the message that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded. POL-RD-23 holds that a reroute is traffic-justified only where the traffic data for the recommended route shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and expressly that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's 'AYE jam already' is therefore bare assertion, and the rider's own account on file — that the AYE looked clear past the slip road — is what the data supports.

The only advisory of an admissible type in the record is the lane-1 roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah. Pasir Panjang Road and Telok Blangah Road are roads on the route the driver actually took, not on the recommended route, which the trip record lists as Clementi Avenue 2, Ayer Rajah Expressway, Keppel Road and Wallich Street. POL-RD-23 requires an advisory that intersects the recommended route; a closure on the road chosen instead cannot excuse leaving the AYE, and the derived read of that artifact itself leaves intersections with the route undetermined rather than shown.

The chat log shows the driver asked 'AYE jam already, I go West Coast Highway can?' and the rider answered 'ok'. That satisfies at most the informed-and-agreed limb of POL-RD-24 row (a), which also requires the reroute to have been traffic-justified; the LTA record for the AYE shows no congestion, incident or closure. On the applicable row — row (d) of POL-RD-24, not traffic-justified and deviation over 1 km — the rider is owed the excess distance fare in full: deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge. That is 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.37 SGD, which is precisely the figure the fare ledger carries both as the excess distance fare and as the amount already refunded to the rider. The driver's recovery claim asks for a figure the matrix says belongs to the rider.

The 1.37 SGD was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings on 19 Aug 2026 at 01:56:34, and the ledger records the payment as partially refunded with 1.37 SGD refund-issued. The driver filed this dispute to claw that sum back. The rider-favourable, record-consistent outcome is therefore that the driver's claim fails and the state as it now stands — the refund with the rider — is preserved, with no amount moved.

Nothing here needs a human reviewer to fill a gap. Driver D-14860 filed to claw back the 1.37 SGD that was refunded to rider R-27563 and recovered from his earnings on 19 Aug 2026 (fare_adjusted). On the record, that refund was correct and the driver's claim fails.

SIZE OF THE DEVIATION. Both sides agree on this and they are right. POL-RD-22 measures deviation as the platform's recorded distances: actual 14.6 km minus recommended 12.7 km = 1.90 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace's own 12.318 km is not used to re-measure it, because POL-RD-22 says a sparse trace understates a route's length. So this is a deviation case, not a tolerance case, and rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 are unavailable to the driver.

TRAFFIC JUSTIFICATION. POL-RD-23 allows a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The record for the recommended route itself — EV-ADVIS-05006-01, the AYE towards the City between Clementi Road and Keppel Viaduct, overlapping the trip window — is type NONE, with speed bands 4-6: no congestion, incident or closure. The driver's argument that the corridor 'was not running free' on those bands and on the 28-42 km/h in his own trace is rejected: POL-RD-23's mapping admits only congestion, incident and closure types, and expressly says a type such as NONE, and a driver's bare assertion of traffic, do not justify a reroute. The only advisory of an admissible type, EV-ADVIS-05006-02 (lane-1 roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah), is on the road the driver chose, not on the recommended route (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street), so it cannot excuse leaving the AYE. The reroute is not traffic-justified.

THE MATRIX AND THE MONEY. Because the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: the rider is owed the excess distance fare in full, being deviation distance times the per-km rate with no surge — 1.90 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.37 SGD, exactly the figure already refunded and recorded in the fare ledger. The driver's row (a) argument (informed and agreed, so no refund) is rejected: row (a) also requires the reroute to have been traffic-justified, and it was not; the rider's 'ok' in the chat log was given on the driver's unverified premise of a jam and cannot convert an unjustified deviation into a no-refund one. The driver's alternative argument — that EV-ADVIS-05006-02's intersection with the route is left undetermined, so the case must go to a human under POL-GEN-26 — is rejected: POL-RD-23 requires the advisory to intersect the recommended route, and a roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road cannot do that, so there is no open question. Nothing here is missing or impaired: every artifact is graded COMPLETE at full weight, so no fact fails for want of evidence and no escalation under POL-GEN-26 arises. The contested amount is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met.

OUTCOME. Read against the driver's filing and the present state, as POL-GEN-03 requires: the rider is owed the 1.37 SGD already refunded, so the driver's claim is not supported and the present state stands — NO_ACTION, with no amount moved and none owed back to the driver. The 1.37 SGD stays with the rider.

The only advisory of an admissible type in the record is the lane-1 roadwork on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah.
